summary:
LunaPilot is an interactive lunar landing site analysis platform designed to help identify and evaluate potential landing locations on the Moon. We developed a web-based application that combines NASA lunar terrain elevation data with solar position information to analyze the environmental conditions of selected landing sites.

The platform allows users to explore lunar regions, examine terrain characteristics, understand sunlight conditions, and compare potential landing locations. By combining these datasets, LunaPilot provides visual insights that can support the assessment of landing site suitability.

Our project addresses the NASA challenge by transforming complex lunar datasets into an accessible, interactive analysis tool. This is important because selecting a safe and suitable lunar landing site is essential for future exploration missions, astronaut safety, and the success of lunar operations. LunaPilot aims to make lunar site evaluation easier to understand and support more informed landing-site decisions.
details:
LunaPilot is an interactive platform that helps users explore, analyze, and compare potential lunar landing sites. It combines NASA's LOLA lunar elevation data with solar position information to examine terrain characteristics and sunlight conditions.

The platform provides an interactive map, terrain visualization, site analysis, and comparison features to make lunar data easier to understand and support better landing-site decisions.

We developed it using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Bootstrap, and PHP, integrating NASA/JPL scientific datasets.

Our innovation is combining terrain and sunlight analysis in one accessible platform. During development, we considered terrain elevation, surrounding topography, sunlight availability, landing-site suitability, data accuracy, and user experience.

Our intended impact is to support safer, more informed lunar exploration by making important environmental information easier to explore and compare.
